newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - June 12.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League defender Brad Wira, from the Western Bulldogs, was suspended for two matches by the Australian Football League Tribunal last night for squeezing another player's testicles. Wira will now be unable to represent Western Australia n their State of Origin match on June 20. Geelong player Gary Hocking told the tribunal Wira had squeezed his testicles for two to three seconds during Saturday's match at Optus Oval, causing him considerable pain. Hocking was suspended for one match for striking Wira after the incident. Page 18.

Fears that the Australian Capital Territory Brumbies rugby union grand final side would be poached by other Super 12 teams have eased with fullback Steve Larkham and Australian centre Adam Magro re-signing yesterday for another two seasons. The new deals mean the Brumbies have secured five of their first-choice backline. Page 17.

Soccer Australia has defended national coach Terry Venables against speculation he might be sacked for an alleged conflict of interest. Venables has sent videos of Australian players to English club Portsmouth, where he is chairman, but Soccer Australia cairman David Hill said the negotiations for a number of players had been with Portsmouth manager Terry Fenwick. Venables is allowed to pursue outside interests as long as he does not become directly involved in the transfer of players. Page 16.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales sealed the Australian Rugby League State of Origin series when it defeated Queensland 15-14 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground last night. New South Wales utility John Simon gave his team the win with a field goal 11 minutes from fulltime. Quensland replacement Julian O'Neill missed a penalty goal which would have won the match with four minutes remaining. Page 48.

The Australian soccer team defeated the Solomon Islands 13-0 at Parramatta Stadium last night in what was expected to be Australia's toughest game of the opening stage of their World Cup campaign. The scoreline was the biggest in Australia's history, with strikers Damien Mori and John Aloisi scoring five goals each. Page 47.

Australian Olympics Committee head John Coates has given his support for women's water polo to be included in the Sydney 2000 Olympics. Coates said he was disappointed that the International Swimming Federation has decided to include an extra women's synchronised swimming event rather than women's water polo. The Australian world champion women's water polo team has threatened legal action over the exclusion of the sport on the grounds of sexual discrimination. Page 47.
THE AGE

Geelong Australian Football League player Gary Ablett's playing career is likely to end when he has a partial knee reconstruction in two weeks. Ablett's manager Ricky Nixon and Geelong are keen to convince him not to play next season, but Ablett is keen to continue, at a different club if necessary, despite media and ambassadorial offers. Page C18.

St Kilda Australian Football League player Nicky Winmar will play in reserve grade against Carlton on Sunday, after going missing from the club with personal problems for the past week-and-a-half. Winmar is believed to be having difficulty gaining access to his children, who live with his estranged wife. Club officials said they would not take disciplinary action given the circumstances, but would make Winmar earn back his senior team position. Page C18.

The South East Melbourne Magic basketball team defeated a flu-ridden Canberra Cannons 80-55 at Melbourne Park last night, holding Canberra to the lowest score in the National Basketball League's 18-year history. The Cannons scored only four points in the ourth quarter. Page C17.
THE HERALD SUN

Essendon Australian Football League player Michael Long underwent arthroscopic surgery to stem the bleeding in his right knee yesterday, which was a complication of the reconstructive surgery he underwent after damaging his anterior cruciate ligament in Rund 8. Long is still on schedule to resume playing in the first round of the season next year. Page 84.

Victorian cricket officials remain confident they can lure Tasmanian vice-captain and opening batsman Jamie Cox to the Bushrangers next season, following talks that both parties described as positive. A formal offer will be made by the end of next week. Pge 82.

Australian cyclist Matthew Atkins has allegedly tested positive to testosterone while riding in Belgium. A positive reading normally brings an automatic six month penalty, but because the hormone occurs naturally in the body, Atkins will undergo further tsts to determine his normal level. Page 79.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Sutherland defeated the Australian Institute of Sport 69-53 in the eighth round of the Dairy Farmers State Netball League in Sydney last night. Sutherland moved to within striking distance of league leaders Parramatta Auburn, with last night's victory givng them a 6-2 win/loss record. Page 79.

Relations between world 500cc motorcycle champion Michael Doohan and fellow Australian rider Anthony Gobert have soured following Doohan's victory in the French Grand Prix when Gobert accused Doohan of dirty tactics. Gobert claimed Doohan ran him off the rack during the first qualifying session for the race. Page 69.

Star Super League players Laurie Daley and Brett Mullins will return to the Canberra Raiders team for Sunday's World Club Challenge match against the London Broncos at Bruce Stadium in Canberra. Daley and Mullins missed Canberra's 70-6 victory over Halifa last weekend with injuries, but their return will see the Raiders at full strength. Page 76.
